summary: Researched 2026-08-22 with live fetches. Key findings: (1) api.weather.gov raw gridpoints (2.5 km) expose quantitativePrecipitation (mm), snowfallAmount (mm), iceAccumulation (mm), snowLevel (m MSL), probabilityOfPrecipitation (%), temperature/dewpoint (degC) as ISO-8601 interval time series to ~8 days; alerts filter by area=WA or zone=WAZ311/WAC057; text products (AFD/ESF/FLW/FLS/FFA/RVF/HYD...) are retained ~7 days; User-Agent mandatory; rate limit undisclosed. (2) NBM is now v5.0 (operational May 5, 2026, SCN 26-24): s3://noaa-nbm-grib2-pds/blend.YYYYMMDD/HH/{core,qmd,text}/; CONUS core f001-f264 (hourly to 48, 3-h to 192, 6-h to 264); core carries APCP/ASNOW (1-h, 6-h) with exceedance probabilities and percentiles, and a SNOWLVL element (wet-bulb 0.5 C height, deterministic + 1-99 percentiles); qmd carries APCP percentiles 0-99 and exceedance probabilities; observed latency ~72-78 min. (3) HRRR (v4, 3 km, hourly; 48 h at 00/06/12/18Z, else 18 h; 15-min wrfsubh): wrfsfc has APCP, PRATE, ASNOW, WEASD, FROZR, HGT at 0C isotherm and highest tropospheric freezing level, TMP/DPT 2 m, PWAT, SSRUN/BGRUN; observed latency ~53 min for f01. RRFS/REFS go operational Oct 6, 2026; HRRR keeps running as a REFS member but has no published retirement date. (4) GFS pgrb2.0p25 (hourly to f120, 3-h to f384) includes SPFH/UGRD/VGRD on 41 pressure levels plus APCP, PWAT, 0C-isotherm height -- everything needed to compute IVT; GEFS (31 members, 0.5 deg, 3-h to f240, 6-h to f384, 00Z to f840) needs pgrb2b for SPFH -- pgrb2a only has RH/limited winds; no NOAA pre-computed IVT products exist. (5) CW3E AR Scale (Ralph et al. 2019: max IVT 250/500/750/1000/1250 with <24 h demotion, >48 h promotion) and IVT forecast tools (GFS/GEFS/ECMWF/West-WRF) are image-only, 'research purposes only', no public API; NOAA PSL AR portal is also image-only. WPC QPF/ERO are programmatically accessible via ArcGIS REST (mapservices.weather.noaa.gov), GeoJSON (ERO Day1-5), shapefiles and 5-km GRIB2 (ftp-wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/5km_qpf/). (6) Snow level vs freezing level: Seattle broadcast meteorologists (incl. ex-NWS Seattle Ted Buehner) cite ~1,000 ft below the freezing level; NWS research cited by OpenSnow gives ~700 ft average with a 500-1,500 ft range; NBM defines snow level as the wet-bulb 0.5 C height. No weather.gov page stating the 1,000-ft rule was found.

providers.name: NWS API (api.weather.gov) - gridpoint forecasts, alerts, text products
providers.authority: NOAA / National Weather Service (forecasts from WFO Seattle SEW, Spokane OTX, Portland PQR, Pendleton PDT; hydrologic text from NWRFC via issuing office PTR)

access.mechanism: REST/JSON over HTTPS. Point lookup /points/{lat},{lon} returns gridId/gridX/gridY and links to /gridpoints/{wfo}/{x},{y} (raw numerical grid), /forecast (12-h periods), /forecast/hourly, plus forecastZone/county/fireWeatherZone URLs. Alerts: /alerts/active?area=WA, /alerts/active?zone=WAZ311 (forecast zone) or ?zone=WAC057 (county), /alerts/active/zone/{zoneId}, /alerts (history with start/end/cursor/limit). Text products: /products/types, /products/types/{typeId}/locations/{locationId}, .../latest (includes productText), /products?type=AFD&office=KSEW&start=&end=&limit=. OpenAPI spec at https://api.weather.gov/openapi.json.
access.auth: None. A User-Agent header is required to identify the application (documented format: 'User-Agent: (myweatherapp.com, contact@myweatherapp.com)'); requests without one are refused.
access.rate_limits: Documented only as 'reasonable rate limits ... a generous amount for typical use'; exceeded requests return an error and 'may be retried after the limit clears (typically within 5 seconds)'. No numeric limit published. Observed response header on /alerts/active: Cache-Control: public, max-age=5. No X-RateLimit headers observed.

providers.cadence: Gridpoint data refresh whenever the WFO publishes a new grid (observed updateTime 2026-08-22T06:26Z for SEW; typically several times per day). Alerts are near-real-time. AFD issued ~3-4x/day by SEW (observed 28 AFDs in 7 days).
providers.latency: Minutes after WFO publication (not documented numerically). Alerts endpoint cache max-age=5 s.
providers.spatial_resolution: 2.5 km NDFD grid (OpenAPI description: 'Returns raw numerical forecast data for a 2.5km grid area'). Alerts are polygons/UGC zones (forecast zones WAZxxx, counties WACxxx).
providers.temporal_resolution: Raw gridpoint values are ISO-8601 interval-valued (e.g. validTime '2026-08-22T00:00:00+00:00/PT6H'): observed quantitativePrecipitation/snowfallAmount/iceAccumulation in PT6H blocks, snowLevel PT3H, probabilityOfPrecipitation PT2H-PT12H, temperature PT1H-PT2H. Hourly forecast endpoint is hourly; /forecast is 12-h periods.
providers.historical_depth: Forecasts: none (only current grid; validTimes extent observed P8DT1H ~ 8 days). Alerts: /alerts supports start/end history queries. Text products: observed retention ~7 days (oldest KSEW AFD and oldest FLW in /products on 2026-08-22 were 2026-08-15).
providers.missing_data_semantics: Gridpoint properties present but with empty 'values' arrays when the element is not populated (observed: hainesIndex, lightningActivityLevel, pressure, wave fields with n=0); uom is null for non-numeric elements (weather, hazards). Alerts: empty features array when none active. Products: '@graph' empty list when no product issued in retention window (observed ESF/RVF at PTR count=0 in August).
providers.quality_flags: None in gridpoint data. Alerts carry status (actual/exercise/test), messageType (alert/update/cancel), severity, certainty, urgency, and VTEC in parameters.
providers.units: WMO unit codes: wmoUnit:degC, wmoUnit:percent, wmoUnit:mm (quantitativePrecipitation, snowfallAmount, iceAccumulation), wmoUnit:m (snowLevel, elevation), wmoUnit:km_h-1 (wind), wmoUnit:degree_(angle).
providers.licensing: U.S. Government work; no license statement on the API docs page (INFERENCE: public domain). NWS abusive-user policy allows IP blocking of clients that impair service; contact sdm@noaa.gov.
limitations: No numeric rate limit published; design polling around product refresh cycles per the NWS abusive-user guidance.
Grid mappings occasionally change; docs say to re-check /points periodically rather than caching gridX/gridY forever.

Text product retention is only ~7 days (observed), so an archive must be built by polling; ESF (Flood Potential Outlook), FLW/FLS/FFA for SEW/PTR were absent in the August window and will only appear when issued.
snowLevel is provided as a WFO-edited grid (m MSL) with no definition of the underlying method in the API.
Alerts endpoints do not carry SPC SEL language for tornado watches (documented); irrelevant to hydrology but shows product text is not embedded in alerts.
Product-type catalog lists QPF code with only 1 issuing location nationally; WPC QPF should come from WPC services, not this API.

evidence.claim: User-Agent required; rate limits 'reasonable' and undisclosed; retry typically within 5 seconds; formats GeoJSON/JSON-LD/DWML/CAP/OXML/ATOM; /points and /gridpoints endpoints; re-check /points periodically

Raw gridpoint properties include quantitativePrecipitation (wmoUnit:mm, PT6H), snowfallAmount (mm), iceAccumulation (mm), snowLevel (wmoUnit:m, PT3H), probabilityOfPrecipitation (percent), temperature/dewpoint (degC), validTimes P8DT1H
Sedro-Woolley 48.50,-122.24 maps to SEW grid 136,109; forecastZone WAZ311; county WAC057; fire zone WAZ656; radar KATX

OpenAPI: /gridpoints returns 'raw numerical forecast data for a 2.5km grid area'; /alerts/active params status, message_type, event, code, area, point, region, region_type, zone (forecast or county), urgency, severity, certainty; /alerts adds start, end, limit, cursor; /products params location, start, end, office, wmoid, type, limit

Alert feature properties: event, severity, urgency, certainty, status, messageType, areaDesc, sent/effective/onset/expires/ends, headline, description, instruction, geocode.SAME/UGC, affectedZones, parameters.NWSheadline/VTEC
?zone=WAC057 (Skagit County) filter works and titles 'Current watches, warnings, and advisories for Skagit County (WAC057) WA'; /alerts/active/zone/WAZ568 returns 200; Cache-Control max-age=5

Product codes: AFD, HWO, ESF=Flood Potential Outlook, FLW=Flood Warning, FLS=Flood Statement, FFA/FFW/FFS/FFG, RVF=River Forecast, RVA, RVS, RVD, HYD=Daily Hydrometeorological Products, ESP/ESG/ESS, QPF, HMD, AHD
SEW recently issued AFD, QPS, PFM, ZFP, RR*, HML etc.; PTR (NWRFC) issued HYD, FTP, RR1-3, RRS; OTX issued AFD, FLS, FZL (Freezing Level Data/RADAT)
Oldest retained KSEW AFD on 2026-08-22 was issued 2026-08-15 (28 products); oldest FLW nationally 2026-08-15 -> ~7-day retention
Retention is a fixed 7-day window
NWS may block IPs impacting service; align requests to data refresh cycles; contact sdm@noaa.gov

providers.relevance_to_cascadia_papsukkal: Primary source for official WFO-edited QPF, snow amount and snow level grids at 2.5 km for every WA basin, for flood watches/warnings by county/zone (Skagit WAC057, etc.), and for AFD/ESF/FLW/FLS/RVF narrative text. Poll gridpoints per basin centroid/elevation band and archive text products daily to build history.

providers.name: National Blend of Models (NBM) v5.0 GRIB2 on AWS Open Data / NOMADS
providers.authority: NOAA / NWS Meteorological Development Laboratory (MDL); disseminated via NCEP Central Operations and NOAA Open Data Dissemination (NODD)

access.mechanism: Anonymous S3 (HTTPS GET / aws s3 --no-sign-request). Prefix: blend.YYYYMMDD/HH/core/blend.tHHz.core.fFFF.RR.grib2 and .../qmd/blend.tHHz.qmd.fFFF.RR.grib2 (RR = co, ak, hi, pr, gu, oc, global), each with a .idx sidecar for byte-range subsetting; text bulletins under blend.YYYYMMDD/HH/text/blend_nb{h,s,e,x,p}tx.tHHz. Also NOMADS https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/blend/prod/blend.YYYYMMDD/CC/{core,qmd,text}/ and grib filter https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/filter_blend.pl. SNS new-object notifications available (Lambda/SQS only). A COG (GeoTIFF) mirror exists in s3://noaa-nbm-pds.
access.auth: None (public bucket; --no-sign-request). NOMADS: none but subject to 120 hits/min per IP.
access.rate_limits: AWS: none documented. NOMADS: 120 hits/minute per IP across NCEP sites (SCN 21-32, effective 2021-04-20).

providers.cadence: Runs every hour (24 cycles/day); each cycle produces output to 264 h (SCN 26-24). Observed on AWS: every hour 00-23Z present.
providers.latency: Observed for the 2026-08-21 12Z cycle (CONUS core): f001 landed 13:12:41Z (+72 min), f036 13:14:34Z, f264 13:18:28Z (+78 min). SCN 26-24 warns v5.0 changed timing for some qmd/core products (some later, some earlier); MDL publishes an 'NBMv5.0 Timing Differences' document.
providers.spatial_resolution: CONUS 2.5 km NDFD grid (INFERENCE; not re-verified on a fetched page). Domains: co, ak, hi, pr, gu, oc, global (observed in bucket).
providers.temporal_resolution: CONUS core (observed 12Z 2026-08-21): f001-f264 with 1-h steps to f048, 3-h steps f048-f192, 6-h steps f192-f264 (108 files). CONUS qmd: files present for every hour f001-f276 (276 files; element content per hour varies). Precip: APCP 1-h (e.g. '23-24 hour acc') and 6-h ('18-24 hour acc') windows in core; qmd percentiles for 6/12/24/48/72-h windows per NBM element list.
providers.historical_depth: AWS GRIB2 archive begins blend.20200518 (observed earliest prefix). NOMADS keeps 1-2 days only (nbm-download page). Note version discontinuities: v4.0 2020-09-29, v4.1 2023-01-17, v4.2 2024-05-15, v4.3 2025-04-15, v5.0 2026-05-05.
providers.missing_data_semantics: GRIB2 bitmap/missing values; percentile records are labeled e.g. 'ASNOW:surface:18-24 hour acc@(fcst,dt=6 hour),missing=0:50% level' (missing treated as 0 in the accumulation aggregation). Only a subset of elements exists at each forecast hour (e.g. 6-h accumulations only at hours divisible by 6); absence of a record in the .idx means not produced for that hour, not a data outage.
providers.quality_flags: None per-record. Probabilistic spread available via 'ens std dev' records (e.g. DPT:2 m above ground:ens std dev) and percentile/exceedance records.
providers.units: GRIB2 SI: APCP/ASNOW/FICEAC in kg m-2 (= mm liquid / m snow per GRIB convention; ASNOW thresholds observed as 0.0254, 0.0508 ... m i.e. 1, 2 inches), SNOWLVL in m above MSL, TMP/DPT in K, PWAT kg m-2, WIND m s-1.
providers.licensing: NODD: 'NOAA data disseminated through NODD are open to the public and can be used as desired'; attribution for unaltered data requested; modified data must be labeled as such; no implied NOAA endorsement.
limitations: NBM v5.0 (May 5, 2026) changed element mix and timing vs v4.3; pipelines written against 2025 documentation need re-validation (hourly guidance now to 48 h; Haines Index removed; new 24-h PMM QPF and 24/48/72-h calibrated snow exceedance products; new PWAT).
No freezing-level (0C isotherm height) element observed in the CONUS core f024 index; NBM provides SNOWLVL (wet-bulb 0.5 C height) instead. Use HRRR/GFS HGT:0C isotherm for freezing level.
Full CONUS files are large; use .idx byte-range subsetting (Herbie) for a WA window rather than downloading whole files.
NOMADS retains only 1-2 days of NBM; AWS is the archive.

Percentile and exceedance records use GRIB2 local-table encodings that older cfgrib/eccodes tables may not name correctly (one unnamed record observed: 'var discipline=0 center=7 local_table=1 parmcat=0 parm=206').

evidence.claim: Buckets arn:aws:s3:::noaa-nbm-grib2-pds (GRIB2) and arn:aws:s3:::noaa-nbm-pds (COG), us-east-1; updated hourly; NODD license text; SNS notifications
Bucket layout blend.YYYYMMDD/HH/{core,qmd,text}/, regions co/ak/hi/pr/gu/oc/global, earliest prefix blend.20200518, text files blend_nbetx/nbhtx/nbptx/nbstx/nbxtx.t12z
CONUS core 12Z cycle: f001-f264, 1-h to f048, 3-h to f192, 6-h to f264; qmd f001-f276 hourly files; LastModified f001 13:12:41Z, f264 13:18:28Z

Core f024 CONUS index contains APCP (1-h and 6-h acc, deterministic + prob >0.254), ASNOW (1-h/6-h deterministic, exceedance probs, 1-99% percentiles), FICEAC, SNOWLVL deterministic ('0 m above mean sea level') plus SNOWLVL percentiles 1-99%, SNOWLR, PTYPE probabilities, TMP/DPT/RH 2 m, TMIN, APTMP, WIND/GUST, PWAT, CAPE; 216 records; no HGT:0C isotherm record

qmd f024 CONUS index: 327 records; APCP 18-24 h exceedance probabilities (>0.254, 2.54, 6.35, 12.7, 25.4, 38.1, 50.8, 63.5, 76.2, 127 mm) and percentiles 0-95% in 5% steps; also TMP, DPT, RH, WIND, GUST, APTMP, HTSGW, JFWPRB

NBM snow level element defined as 'Elevation where the wet bulb temperature reaches 0.5 degrees C'; QPF01/06 to 264 h; PoP01/06/12; PctQPF06/12/24/48/72 percentiles 1-99 in QMD; SnowAmt01/06/24/48/72; PctSnow; ProbSnow; PType; snow ratio
Version 5.0 is current operational as of May 5, 2026 (update July 28, 2026 for temperature issues); v4.3 2025-04-15; v4.2 2024-05-15
NCO change log lists NBM v5.0 implementation May 5, 2026

SCN 26-24 (updated AAC): effective on/about April 30, 2026 13Z with CWD fallback; NBM runs hourly producing output to 264 h; hourly guidance extended from 36 to 48 h; new 24-h PMM QPF and snow/ice (CO, AK); new 24/48/72-h calibrated snow exceedance (CO); new deterministic/probabilistic PWAT; Haines Index removed; dissemination timing changes; parallel data at nomads .../blend/para/
NOMADS paths .../blend/prod/blend.YYYYMMDD/CC/core/ and /qmd/ and /text/; AWS index URL; retention on NOMADS 1-2 days; file naming blend.tCCz.{core,qmd}.fXXX.RR.grib2
https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/filter_blend.pl returns HTTP 200
CONUS grid spacing is 2.5 km

providers.relevance_to_cascadia_papsukkal: Best single calibrated, probabilistic QPF/snow source for WA basins out to 11 days: 6-h APCP percentiles and exceedance probabilities (qmd) give rain-on-snow and flood-volume uncertainty directly; SNOWLVL percentiles give snow-line uncertainty per basin; hourly steps to 48 h match flashy west-slope basins. Subset a WA bounding box via .idx byte ranges each hour.

providers.name: HRRR (High-Resolution Rapid Refresh) on AWS Open Data (noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds)
providers.authority: NOAA NCEP (run by NCO; developed by NOAA GSL); NODD distribution

access.mechanism: Anonymous S3. Prefix hrrr.YYYYMMDD/conus/hrrr.tHHz.{wrfsfc,wrfprs,wrfnat,wrfsubh}fFF.grib2 (+.idx); hrrr.YYYYMMDD/alaska/ for AK. Also NOMADS https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/hrrr/prod/ and grib filter https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/filter_hrrr_2d.pl. Zarr mirror s3://hrrrzarr (us-west-1, University of Utah). SNS topic arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123901341784:NewHRRRObject.
access.rate_limits: AWS: none documented. NOMADS: 120 hits/min per IP.

providers.cadence: Hourly cycles (24/day); radar data assimilated every 15 min.
providers.temporal_resolution: Hourly output; 00/06/12/18Z cycles run to 48 h (observed 49 files f00-f48 for wrfsfc/wrfprs/wrfnat at 12Z), other cycles to 18 h (observed 13Z wrfsfc max f18). wrfsubh: 15-min fields (each file holds HH and 15/30/45 min before) to 18 h only (observed 19 files at 12Z).
providers.historical_depth: AWS archive from hrrr.20140730 (observed earliest prefix) to present; early years are pre-HRRRv4 (v4 operational 2020-12-02).
providers.missing_data_semantics: GRIB2 bitmap. Accumulation records carry explicit windows ('0-6 hour acc', '5-6 hour acc'); sub-hourly APCP windows are '300-315 min acc'. f00 has no accumulation.
providers.units: APCP kg m-2 (mm), PRATE kg m-2 s-1, ASNOW m, WEASD kg m-2, SNOD m, HGT m (geopotential height of 0C isotherm / highest tropospheric freezing level), TMP/DPT K, PWAT kg m-2, SSRUN/BGRUN kg m-2.
providers.licensing: NODD public; attribution requested; no endorsement claims.
limitations: 18-h horizon for 20 of 24 cycles; only 48 h at synoptic cycles -- short lead for multi-day AR events.
Full CONUS files are ~100+ MB; subset via .idx/Herbie to a WA window.

RRFS/REFS become operational 2026-10-06 12 UTC (SCN 26-48); HRRR continues (it supplies two REFS members) but NOAA has signalled eventual retirement with no published date -- plan an RRFS migration path (parallel feed on NOMADS since 2026-08-11 at .../rrfs/para/).
rapidrefresh.noaa.gov is behind Cloudflare bot protection (403 to automated fetches); rely on NCO product pages and the AWS registry for docs.
0C-isotherm height and 'highest tropospheric freezing level' are model freezing levels, not snow levels; apply a snow-level offset or use wet-bulb from wrfprs.

evidence.claim: Buckets noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds (us-east-1, archive since 2014) and hrrrzarr (us-west-1, Univ. of Utah); hourly; 3-km, hourly updated, radar assimilation every 15 min; NODD license wording
SNS topic arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123901341784:NewHRRRObject; s3://noaa-hrrr-bdp-pds

Families wrfprs (3D pressure), wrfnat (native), wrfsfc (2D surface), wrfsubh (sub-hourly: HH plus 15/30/45 min before); 00/06/12/18Z to 48 h, others 18 h; sub-hourly stays 18 h; naming hrrr.tCCz.[product]FF.[ak].grib2

12Z 2026-08-21: 49 wrfsfc/wrfprs/wrfnat files (f00-f48), 19 wrfsubh (f00-f18); 13Z wrfsfc max f18; alaska/ and conus/ prefixes; earliest prefix hrrr.20140730; LastModified f01 12:53Z, f18 13:13Z, f48 13:46Z

wrfsfcf06 index (173 records) includes APCP 0-6 h and 5-6 h acc, PRATE, ASNOW, WEASD, SNOD, SNOWC, FROZR, FRZR, CSNOW/CICEP/CFRZR/CRAIN, TMP/DPT 2 m, TMP surface, PWAT, HGT:0C isotherm, RH:0C isotherm, HGT:highest tropospheric freezing level, SSRUN, BGRUN, REFC
wrfsubhf06 index has APCP 15-min accumulations (300-315, 315-330, 330-345, 345-360 min) and PRATE at 315/330/345/360 min
HRRR v4.0 and RAP v5.0 implemented December 2, 2020

SCN 26-48 (updated AAB, 2026-07-06): RRFS/REFS effective October 6, 2026; RRFS hourly, North America at 3 km; replaces NAM, HREF, SREF, HiresW (retirements in SCN 26-47); HRRR provides two additional REFS members (current and 6-h-old cycles) for CONUS and Alaska; parallel feed from Aug 11, 2026 at nomads .../rrfs/para/ and .../refs/para/
RRFS 00/06/12/18Z cycles to 84 h, other hourly cycles to 18 h; public S3 bucket noaa-rrfs-ops-pds for the parallel feed
Date on which HRRR itself will be retired

providers.relevance_to_cascadia_papsukkal: Highest-resolution operational QPF, precipitation type, 15-min rain rates, freezing-level height and surface/baseflow runoff proxies for orographic west-slope basins (Skagit, Nooksack, Snoqualmie, Cedar, Green, Puyallup/White) at 0-18/48 h. Use for nowcast-range AR intensity and rain/snow partition; pair with NBM/GFS/GEFS for longer leads.

providers.name: GFS (Global Forecast System) 0.25-degree GRIB2 on AWS Open Data / NOMADS

access.mechanism: Anonymous S3: gfs.YYYYMMDD/HH/atmos/gfs.tHHz.pgrb2.0p25.fFFF (+.idx); also pgrb2.0p50, pgrb2.1p00, goessimpgrb2 families observed in the bucket. NOMADS directory https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/pub/data/nccf/com/gfs/prod/ and grib filters https://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/filter_gfs_0p25.pl and filter_gfs_0p25_1hr.pl (subset by variable, level, lat/lon box).
access.rate_limits: AWS: none documented. NOMADS: 120 hits/min per IP (SCN 21-32).

providers.spatial_resolution: 0.25 deg lat/lon output grid (registry: ~28 km base, ~70 km beyond one week).
providers.temporal_resolution: Observed: hourly f000-f120, then 3-hourly to f384 (209 files). APCP windows are cumulative from f000 ('0-6 hour acc') with 6-h reset buckets in GFS convention.
providers.historical_depth: AWS bucket prefixes start gfs.20210101 (observed); 0.25-deg GRIB2 from 2021. Older GFS history requires NCEI/other archives.
providers.missing_data_semantics: GRIB2 bitmap. f000 has no APCP. Accumulated and averaged variants coexist (APCP acc, PRATE ave, CSNOW/CRAIN both instantaneous and 0-6 h ave).
providers.units: SPFH kg kg-1, UGRD/VGRD m s-1, HGT gpm, APCP kg m-2, PRATE kg m-2 s-1, PWAT kg m-2, TMP/DPT K.
providers.licensing: NODD public; attribution requested; modified data must be labeled.
limitations: No pre-computed IVT or IWV-transport product: IVT must be integrated from SPFH, UGRD, VGRD on pressure levels (1000-300 hPa typical) per grid point.

pgrb2b.0p25 (less-common parameters) was not present in the AWS atmos/ listing for the 12Z 2026-08-21 cycle (observed absence); pgrb2.0p25 already holds SPFH/UGRD/VGRD on 41 levels so it is not needed for IVT.

GFS v17 (9-km coupled system) has been proposed for October 2026 with product/naming changes and removal of some legacy products -- third-party report; official SCN not yet seen. Re-validate file paths at cutover.
Coarse 0.25 deg grid smooths Cascade/Olympic orography; use for synoptic AR/IVT and freezing level, not basin QPF.

evidence.claim: Bucket arn:aws:s3:::noaa-gfs-bdp-pds (us-east-1); 4x/day every 6 h; 16-day horizon; ~28 km base resolution, 70 km beyond one week; NODD license text
Families pgrb2.0p25 (most common params), pgrb2b.0p25 (least common), pgrb2.0p50, pgrb2.1p00, pgrb2full.0p50, sfluxgrb; FFF 000-384; cycles 00/06/12/18

12Z 2026-08-21 pgrb2.0p25: 209 files f000-f384, 1-h steps to f120 then 3-h; other families present: pgrb2.0p50 (129), pgrb2.1p00 (60), goessimpgrb2; pgrb2b.0p25 not listed; LastModified f006 15:36Z, f120 16:09Z, f384 17:16Z; earliest prefix gfs.20210101

providers.name: Snow level vs freezing level relationship (NWS Seattle forecast practice reference)
providers.authority: NWS Seattle (WFO SEW) practice as described by Seattle broadcast meteorologists (Morgan Palmer, KIRO 7; Ted Buehner, KIRO Newsradio, formerly NWS Seattle) and NWS research summarized by OpenSnow; NBM element definition from NWS MDL

access.mechanism: Reference knowledge, not a data feed. Operational inputs: NWS gridpoint snowLevel (m MSL), NBM SNOWLVL (wet-bulb 0.5 C height), HRRR/GFS/GEFS HGT at 0C isotherm and 'highest tropospheric freezing level', OTX FZL (RADAT freezing-level) text product, and twice-daily balloon freezing levels at Forks (UIL) and Spokane (OTX).

providers.spatial_resolution: Not applicable; relationship varies with precipitation intensity and low-level humidity.
providers.units: Feet (broadcast rule of thumb); metres in NWS API and GRIB products.
providers.licensing: Third-party articles are copyrighted; use the numbers, not the text.
limitations: No weather.gov page stating the '1,000 ft below freezing level' rule was found; the NWS Seattle mountain page discusses freezing levels (balloon soundings at Forks/Spokane; highest freezing level shown if multiple) but does not define the offset.

NWS research cited by OpenSnow gives a smaller mean offset (~700 ft) with a 500-1,500 ft range; heavy precipitation and dry low-level air push the snow level further below the freezing level (melting cooling / evaporative cooling).
Model 'freezing level' fields (0C isotherm height) should be converted to snow level with an offset or, better, by computing the wet-bulb 0.5 C height (NBM definition) from model T/RH profiles.

evidence.claim: KIRO 7 chief meteorologist Morgan Palmer: snow level approximately 1,000 ft below the freezing level because snow takes on average about 1,000 ft of above-freezing air to melt; varies with precipitation amount/intensity; 'generally the rule of thumb'
Ted Buehner (KIRO Newsradio, former NWS Seattle): 'The snow level is usually around 1,000 feet lower than the freezing level'; freezing level used when dry, snow level when precipitation is forecast

'According to research conducted by National Weather Service scientists, the snow level, on average, is about 700 feet lower than the freezing level, with a typical range of anywhere from 500 to 1,500 feet below the freezing level'
NWS Seattle mountain page: freezing levels measured twice daily at Forks and Spokane by balloon; if multiple freezing levels, the highest is shown; page gives no snow-level offset
NBM snow level = elevation where wet-bulb temperature reaches 0.5 C
